name: softmax
summary: row softmax of x[R][D]: y = exp(x - max) / sum(exp(x - max))

y.why: reference.py returns an absolute per-element bound y_j R_j as the scale (rtol 1), in float64 from the exact inputs. a_k = x_k - m (m the row max, exact). The f32 subtraction rounds once: d_k = a_k(1+delta), so exp(d_k) = exp(a_k) exp(a_k delta) with |exp(a_k delta) - 1| <= exp(u|a_k|) - 1 (|a_k| <= 60 here: WolframLanguageEvaluator: (Exp[60 u]-1)/u, u=2^-24 -> 60.0001). exp budget 3 ulp (OpenCL C 3.0 s7.4; CUDA expf 2 ulp; Omega rounds a binary64 exp once) = 6u relative (WolframLanguageEvaluator: 3*2^-23/2^-24 -> 6), so e_k^ = e_k(1+eta_k), |eta_k| <= eps_k = (1+6u)exp(u|a_k|) - 1, E = max_k eps_k. The sum of D positive terms in any order: S^ = S(1+theta), |theta| <= (1+E)(1+gamma(D-1)) - 1. The normalisation (divide, or reciprocal then multiply) costs gamma(2). R_j = max((1+eps_j)(1+gamma(2)) / ((1-E)(1-gamma(D-1))) - 1, 1 - (1-eps_j)(1-gamma(2)) / ((1+E)(1+gamma(D-1)))). Inputs are uniform in [-30,30], so every e_k >= exp(-60) is a normal f32 (WolframLanguageEvaluator: Exp[-60] -> 8.7565e-27 > 2^-126 = 1.1755e-38). A kernel without max subtraction is wrong on the softmax_unstable control (inputs in [80,100]).
